title: Cocartesian comparison for the inverse image of an inner horn
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, standard simplices and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $q:\mathcal C\to\Delta^N$ be an inner fibration from a quasicategory and let $0<i<N$. Assume that for every $x\in\mathcal C_{i-1}$ there is a $q$-cocartesian edge $x\to y$ with $y\in\mathcal C_i$, lying over the edge $i-1\to i$. Then
$$\mathcal C\times_{\Delta^N}\Lambda_i^N\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$
is a categorical equivalence and a monomorphism. No cocartesian lifts over other edges of $\Delta^N$ and no colimits in $\mathcal C$ are assumed.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, printed p. 307 and its proof; used in Lemma 3.1.3.16, printed p. 347. Nonsymmetric formulation following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4 Appendix A. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Write $p$ for the given map and $H_i=p^{-1}\Lambda_i^N$. Since pullbacks are degreewise, the inclusion $H_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal C$ is a monomorphism. Every simplicial map from a quasicategory to a standard simplex is inner: fill the horn in the total quasicategory, and its image must be the prescribed base simplex, since an inner horn in a standard simplex has a unique filler. Restrictions over faces are quasicategories and inner fibrations by the same horn argument. A cocartesian edge remains cocartesian under restriction to a face containing its base edge, directly by its lifting definition. All objects of the Joyal model structure are cofibrant because the empty-set inclusions are monomorphisms. Thus the all-cofibrant left-properness lemma applies: pushout along any monomorphism preserves categorical equivalences. These observations will justify the restrictions and pushouts below.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, preliminary pullback and model-category facts used in both filtrations, printed pp. 307–309.

proof.text: First prove the assertion for $i=1$, by strong induction on $N\geq2$, with the $N=2$ case proved in Step 4. For $N>2$, order all nondegenerate simplices containing $0,1$ and at least one further vertex as $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m$ in nonincreasing dimension, with $\sigma_1=\Delta^N$. Let $\sigma_j^0$ be the face omitting vertex $1$, and form $K_j$ by removing $\sigma_k,\sigma_k^0$ and their degeneracies for $k\leq j$, with $K_0=\Delta^N$. A proper coface of a removed $\sigma_k$ is an earlier, larger simplex of the same family. A proper coface of a removed partner $\sigma_k^0$ either contains $1$, hence contains $\sigma_k$, or omits $1$, in which case it is the partner of the earlier, larger simplex obtained by adjoining $1$. Thus every coface of a removed simplex is removed, so $K_j$ is a simplicial subset. The faces of $\sigma_j$ other than $\sigma_j^0$ remain: those containing $0,1$ have smaller dimension, and those omitting $0$ cannot be a removed partner. Thus $K_j\cap\sigma_j=\Lambda_1^{n_j}$, where $n_j=\dim\sigma_j$, and $K_{j-1}=K_j\cup\sigma_j$. Degreewise inverse image takes this union/intersection square to the corresponding pushout square in simplicial sets. For $j>1$, $n_j<N$ and the distinguished consecutive vertices are still $0,1$; restrictions of the stipulated cocartesian lifts satisfy the induction hypothesis. Each map $p^{-1}K_j\to p^{-1}K_{j-1}$ for $j>1$ is therefore a pushout of a categorical equivalence along a monomorphism, hence is a categorical equivalence. Consequently $p^{-1}K_m\to p^{-1}K_1=H_1$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, i=1 descending-dimensional filtration, printed p. 307.

proof.text: Define $c:\Delta^N\to\Delta^2$ by $c(0)=0,c(1)=1,c(k)=2$ for $k>1$. A simplex remains in $K_m$ exactly when its image under $c$ omits $0$ or omits $2$; hence $K_m=c^{-1}\Lambda^2_1$. The composite $cp$ is inner by Step 1. The chosen $p$-cocartesian edges over $0\to1$ are also $cp$-cocartesian: in an outer-horn lifting problem with this first edge, the projected vertices in $\Delta^N$ are ordered, so define a unique base simplex there. For dimension two its last vertex lies over $1$ or $2$ under $c$, hence its original index is at least $1$; in higher dimensions all the necessary adjacent edges are already in the horn. Apply the original cocartesian lifting property over that ordered simplex. Thus Step 4 applied to $cp$ proves $p^{-1}K_m\to\mathcal C$ a categorical equivalence, and two-out-of-three with Step 2 proves $H_1\to\mathcal C$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, collapse to Delta^2, printed p. 307; explicit check of cocartesianness after collapse.

proof.text: For the base case $N=2,i=1$, apply the cocartesian-arrow projection to $p$. The fixed edge $0\to1$ defines $\mathcal C_0\to Z$: every vertex belongs to $Z$ by the lift hypothesis and $Z$ is full. Its pullback is a trivial Kan fibration; choose vertices and lift successive boundaries to obtain a section. This gives $h:\Delta^1\times\mathcal C_0\to\mathcal C$ starting at the inclusion, over $0\to1$, with every vertical edge cocartesian. Apply the prism-comparison lemma to this $p,h$. With $D=\mathcal C_{12}$ and its pushouts $A,B$ as stated there, it gives categorical equivalences $A\to\mathcal C_{01}$ and $B\to\mathcal C$. The map $A\to B$ is a monomorphism: it is the pushout of the degreewise inclusion $\mathcal C_1\hookrightarrow D$. Left properness therefore makes $B\to\mathcal C_{01}\amalg_{\mathcal C_1}D$ a categorical equivalence. Degreewise union and intersection identify this last pushout with $H_1$: the base horn is the union of edges $01,12$ with intersection vertex $1$. Its composite with $H_1\to\mathcal C$ is the prism map $B\to\mathcal C$, since both restrict to $h$ and the inclusion of $D$. Two-out-of-three proves the base case.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, n=2,i=1 prism comparisons, printed p. 308; HTT Definition 3.2.2.6 and Proposition 3.2.2.7(2), printed pp. 180–181, specialized after the explicit collapse and taking opposites.

proof.text: For $i>1$, use strong induction on $N\geq3$, with $N=3,i=2$ proved in Steps 6–7. For $N>3$, use the collapse $c:\Delta^N\to\Delta^3$ and filtration $K_m\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_0$ of the collapse-filtration lemma. For $j>1$ its attaching face has dimension $n_j<N$, with distinguished position $1<p_j<n_j$ and preceding vertex exactly $i-1$. The stipulated cocartesian lifts restrict to that face by Step 1. Degreewise inverse image takes its union/intersection square to a pushout square. Induction on the restricted map and left properness show that each $p^{-1}K_j\to p^{-1}K_{j-1}$ for $j>1$ is a categorical equivalence; their composite gives $p^{-1}K_m\to p^{-1}K_1=H_i$. The lemma identifies $K_m=c^{-1}\Lambda^3_2$. For an outer-horn lifting problem for $cp$ whose first edge is a chosen lift over $i-1\to i$, in dimension two the last original vertex index is at least $i$: its $c$-image is at least $2$, and $c^{-1}(2)=\{i\}$. In higher dimensions the horn already contains every adjacent edge, so the projected original indices are ordered. In either case they determine a unique simplex of $\Delta^N$ extending the projected horn. The $p$-cocartesian lifting property gives a filler over it, and its composite under $c$ is the prescribed simplex, since standard simplices are determined by their vertices. Thus the chosen edges are $cp$-cocartesian. Also $cp$ is inner by Step 1. Apply Steps 6–7 to $cp$ and use two-out-of-three with $p^{-1}K_m\to H_i$ to prove $H_i\to\mathcal C$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, i>1 filtration and collapse, printed pp. 308–309; descending order repairs the explicit source typo.

proof.text: For $N=3,i=2$, let $H=p^{-1}\Lambda^3_2$. The restriction $H\to\Lambda^3_2$ is inner by pullback, and its edges over $1\to2$ remain cocartesian by the lifting definition. Apply the corrected relative-extension lemma to obtain a monomorphism and categorical equivalence $a:H\hookrightarrow\mathcal C'$ with $\mathcal C'$ a quasicategory over $\Delta^3$, whose inverse horn is exactly $H$. The original $p:\mathcal C\to\Delta^3$ is a Joyal fibration: it is inner and every equivalence of the simplex is an identity, lifted by an identity in $\mathcal C$, so characterization (1) applies. The lifting axiom for the trivial cofibration $a$ gives $g:\mathcal C'\to\mathcal C$ over $\Delta^3$ extending $H\hookrightarrow\mathcal C$. Thus $g$ restricts to the identity on the common inverse horn. The map $g$ is obtained here, rather than asserted by the extension lemma.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, n=3,i=2 lifting square, printed p. 309; HA Lemma 3.1.2.4, printed pp. 330–332.

proof.text: The horn $\Lambda^3_2$ contains every vertex and every edge of $\Delta^3$, including degenerate edges. Thus $g$ is bijective on vertices. For any $x,y\in\mathcal C'$, an $n$-simplex of the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C'}(x,y)$ is a simplex $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal C'$ constant at $x$ on its initial $n$-face and with final vertex $y$. Its projection to $\Delta^3$ has vertex sequence $p'(x),\ldots,p'(x),p'(y)$, so factors through a single edge (or is nonexistent if the indices are decreasing). In particular every such simplex lies in the common inverse horn. The identical argument for a mapping simplex in $\mathcal C$ puts it in $H$, where $g$ is the identity, so every such simplex has a unique preimage. The mapping-space operators restrict along the maps $[m+1]\to[n+1]$ preserving the new last vertex; these restrictions in both total spaces are the restrictions in the common simplicial subset $H$. Hence the degreewise bijections commute with every operator, and $g$ is fully faithful. Its full essential image is all of $\mathcal C$ since it is bijective on vertices. The full-essential-image lemma supplies a coherent quasi-inverse; characterization (2) then makes $g$ a categorical equivalence. Finally $H\hookrightarrow\mathcal C=g\circ a$ is a categorical equivalence by two-out-of-three. This finishes the base case, both inductions, and the monomorphism assertion from Step 1.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.6, final right mapping-space argument, printed p. 309; expanded degreewise using the existing mapping-space definition.

lean.statement: theorem cocartesian_inner_horn_comparison (N : ℕ) (i : Fin (N + 1)) (hi : 0 < i) (hiN : i < Fin.last N) (C : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory C] (q : C ⟶ (Δ[N] : SSet.{u})) [InnerFibration q] (hlift : ∀ x : C _⦋0⦌, stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv (q.app (op ⦋0⦌) x) = ⟨i.val - 1, by omega⟩ → ∃ (y : C _⦋0⦌) (e : C _⦋1⦌), C.δ 1 e = x ∧ C.δ 0 e = y ∧ stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv (q.app (op ⦋0⦌) y) = i ∧ SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm e ≫ q = SSet.stdSimplex.map (SimplexCategory.mkOfSucc ⟨i.val - 1, by omega⟩) ∧ IsCocartesianEdge q (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm e)) : (∀ (D : SSet.{max u v}), D.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map (pullback.fst q (horn N i).ι))).app D)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) ∧ Mono (pullback.fst q (horn N i).ι)
